Package com.github.crittscott.somestacks.gametest

Class StoragePileChecks

java.lang.Object
com.github.crittscott.somestacks.gametest.StoragePileChecks
public final class StoragePileChecks extends Object
Storage pile behavior in a live level: deposits filling partial stacks before empty ones, growth when a pile fills, automation insertion addressing the slot it names, obstruction refusing growth, and settling consolidating, packing, and sorting. Player scenarios take the loader's click; automation scenarios take the loader's GameTestScaffold.Automation view.

  • Method Details

    • middleRemovalSettlesAndPublishesBothSurvivingPiles

      public static void middleRemovalSettlesAndPublishesBothSurvivingPiles(net.minecraft.gametest.framework.GameTestHelper helper)
      To reproduce: create a permanent three-block Storage pile and use /data merge block to seed sparse glowstone contents in its end blocks and diamonds in its middle block. Place comparators beside both ends and break the middle before another inventory mutation. Seed two full glowstone stacks below, seven diamonds in the middle, and two single glowstone items above. Only seven diamonds drop. The lower pile packs to two slots (signal 2, light 6); the upper pile merges to one slot (signal 1, light 3). The fixture first drains placement ticks, then seeds sparse local slots and makes a pending upper edit in the removal tick, so it specifically checks rescheduling at the new upper base. That same-tick pending-publication assertion is internal; ordinary deposits pack from the base and cannot create this sparse starting layout. Fixture contents carry a per-run tag so drops from other tests or earlier runs are excluded.

    • depositFillsCompatiblePartialBeforeEmptySlot

      public static void depositFillsCompatiblePartialBeforeEmptySlot(net.minecraft.gametest.framework.GameTestHelper helper)
      Internal deposit-placement check: the fixture seeds 60 stone in local slot 5 and deposits eight more through the block entity, with no player; slot 5 reaches 64 and slot 0 receives four. It pins which slots a deposit fills before settlement, which no click shows.

      The nearest real-trigger check is fullPileGrowsByOneBlock(net.minecraft.gametest.framework.GameTestHelper, java.util.function.Function<net.minecraft.world.item.ItemStack, net.minecraft.server.level.ServerPlayer>, com.github.crittscott.somestacks.gametest.InteractionChecks.LoaderClick). To see the visible part, V-deposit 60 stone into Storage, then eight more in Survival: all eight leave the hand, and one full stack and a four-item remainder occupy the pile.

    • placementChoosesFacingBeforeJoining

      public static void placementChoosesFacingBeforeJoining(net.minecraft.gametest.framework.GameTestHelper helper)
      To reproduce: rotate the top of a Storage pile, then V-place Storage above it or beneath an overhanging pile. New joins inherit the adjacent facing and permanence. Water placement keeps waterlogging. A /setblock with an explicit facing keeps that facing even beside another pile. The fixture also checks that a gap between different facings prefers the block below.

    • settleConsolidatesExactIdentityAndPacksDown

      public static void settleConsolidatesExactIdentityAndPacksDown(net.minecraft.gametest.framework.GameTestHelper helper)
      Internal settlement fixture: directly seed stone stacks of 40 and 30 with {variant:1} and two stacks of five with {variant:2} in separated slots, plus dirt, untagged stone, stone with an explicit empty tag, and two wooden pickaxes with different damage. Settlement orders dirt, untagged stone, tagged stone stacks of 64, 6, and 10, the empty-tag stone (its tag text "{}" sorts after "{variant:...}", and it stays apart from untagged stone), then the pickaxes in ascending damage order.

      For a visible check, /give stone with those tags and deposit the same totals into Storage. Also deposit dirt, untagged stone, and wooden pickaxes with different damage. After settlement, matching tags merge into legal stacks, distinct tags stay separate, and occupied cells pack toward the base in that order. The test's initial gaps require direct fixture writes; source counts and independent output NBT are internal ownership checks.

    • settleMergesOnlyIdenticalNames

      public static void settleMergesOnlyIdenticalNames(net.minecraft.gametest.framework.GameTestHelper helper)
      To reproduce: rename stone "Alpha" and "Beta" in an anvil. Store a full stack of dirt in a Storage Stack, then three Alpha, two Beta, and four Alpha in separate later cells. After settlement the dirt stays in the base cell, the two Alpha stacks merge into one cell of seven, and Beta keeps its own cell of two. The test seeds the separated cells directly; that each written cell holds its own stack, and that the already-settled dirt cell is not rewritten, are internal ownership checks.

    • emptyTemporaryPileDisappearsButPermanentPileRemains

      public static void emptyTemporaryPileDisappearsButPermanentPileRemains(net.minecraft.gametest.framework.GameTestHelper helper)
      To reproduce: place two Storage piles with one item each. Select Toggle Permanent, hold V, and empty-hand right-click one pile. Release V and extract the last item from each. After settlement, the temporary pile disappears while the permanent pile remains empty. The automated fixture starts with empty blocks, invokes settlement directly, and checks that the removed pile reports zero fill and signal and accepts a cleanup request without a base.

    • comparatorReadsTheWholePileFromEveryBlock

      public static void comparatorReadsTheWholePileFromEveryBlock(net.minecraft.gametest.framework.GameTestHelper helper)
      The fixture fills every slot of the lower block of a two-block pile with full stone stacks and leaves the upper block empty, so the pile is half full. Both blocks read 8: a lower-only read would give 15 and an upper-only read 0.

      To reproduce: create a permanent two-block Storage pile by filling until it grows, then toggling permanence. Extract until exactly 27 full stacks remain, which settle into the lower block. Put outward-facing comparators beside both blocks on solid supports; both output 8.

    • ordinaryPlacementBelowPermanentPileRepairsDerivedState

      public static void ordinaryPlacementBelowPermanentPileRepairsDerivedState(net.minecraft.gametest.framework.GameTestHelper helper)
      Internal native-placement check: create a full, permanent Storage block above an empty position with an outward-facing comparator. Its output is 15. Directly place an empty Storage block below it with neighbor updates. After settlement, both blocks remain permanent, contents move into the new base, and the comparator reads 8.

      To reproduce this placement path, prepare the upper pile on a temporary support, fill it, toggle permanence, remove the support, and use /setblock to place somestacks:storage_stack_block below it. Ordinary item deposits do not create the test's empty new base.

    • capabilityInsertionAnswersForTheSlotItIsGiven

      public static void capabilityInsertionAnswersForTheSlotItIsGiven(net.minecraft.gametest.framework.GameTestHelper helper, Function<net.minecraft.world.level.block.entity.BlockEntity,GameTestScaffold.Automation> automation)
      Internal Storage slot check: insert eight stone into local slot 20 through the loader's automation view, reject dirt offered to that now-incompatible slot, then wait for the settlement the insertion scheduled. Before settlement stone occupies slot 20; afterward it occupies slot 0. Simulation and caller-owned input are unchanged.

      To check manually, use slot-addressing automation to insert into an empty Storage slot, then observe the next settlement pack its contents toward the base. Precise pre-tick placement and dry-run results require an automation probe.

      public static void obstructionPreventsGrowthAndSimulationReportsNoRoom(net.minecraft.gametest.framework.GameTestHelper helper, Function<net.minecraft.world.level.block.entity.BlockEntity,GameTestScaffold.Automation> automation)
      To reproduce: fill all 27 slots of a Storage block with full dirt stacks, allow height above one, and put solid stone directly above.       public static void capabilityFromEveryBlockAddressesTheSamePile(net.minecraft.gametest.framework.GameTestHelper helper, Function<net.minecraft.world.level.block.entity.BlockEntity,GameTestScaffold.Automation> automation)
